A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAM2Long and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting a reliable comparison. All pages were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original video segmentation evaluations, parameter ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative comparisons in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original segmentation experiments and adds YouTube-VOS results, tracking evaluations, and computational cost measurements.

M1.justification: The memory-tree search, uncertainty handling, and memory modulation in Section 3 are unchanged. New Section 4.4 adds a tracking adaptation: SAM 2 generates the initial mask from a bounding-box prompt, and subsequent masks become boxes using their nonzero-coordinate extrema.

E1.justification: v2 retains the existing segmentation coverage, adds short-video evaluation on YouTube-VOS in Table 4, and introduces bounding-box single-object tracking on LaSOT, LaSOText, and GOT-10k. This substantially extends the evaluated task requirements and data coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 9 adds 13 tracking comparators, including KeepTrack, TOMP, DropTrack, SeqTrack, MixFormer, GRM-256, ROMTrack, OSTrack, DiffusionTrack, ODTrack, LORAT, DAM2SAM, and SAMURAI, alongside SAM2.1. Comparator membership in the retained segmentation comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added tracking experiments introduce box-based initialization and outputs, AUC evaluation on LaSOT/LaSOText, and AO on GOT-10k. Table 5 also adds GFLOPs measurement. These extend the evaluation design; the retained VOS splits, model configurations, and ablation settings are not reported as revised.

E4.justification: Table 5 extends the existing pathway-count ablation with computational cost, supplementing its accuracy and relative-speed evidence. The other parameter ablations, temporal-performance plots, and qualitative case studies are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, dispersion estimates, or significance tests. The retained algorithmic uncertainty-handling mechanism does not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 9 reports SAM2Long scores of 73.9 and 60.9 AUC on LaSOT and LaSOText, and 81.1 AO on GOT-10k. Table 4 adds a YouTube-VOS tie at 88.7; Table 5 adds 844.1–946.4 GFLOPs across pathway counts. Table 4 removes separate J and F results for its retained datasets. Existing aggregate segmentation and ablation accuracy scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The memory definitions, cumulative log-IoU scoring equation, selection conditions, and attention-weight equations are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or mathematical derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion change the stated coverage of consistent VOS superiority from five to six benchmarks, although v1 already says six elsewhere. The central training-free memory-tree contribution and the claimed 3.0-point average and 5.3-point maximum improvements remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explains the YouTube-VOS tie through its short average duration of 4.5 seconds and interprets the tracking results as competitive with VOT-specialized SAMURAI and DAM2SAM. The existing occlusion explanations and limitation concerning multi-object interactions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 supplies concrete processing instructions for the tracking application: box-prompt mask initialization and conversion of nonzero mask extents to bounding boxes. The existing memory implementation details, hyperparameter descriptions, and code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantial body of tracking-method and benchmark literature and extends its positioning to dedicated visual trackers, particularly the newer SAM 2 adaptations SAMURAI and DAM2SAM. This expansion appears in Section 4.4 and Table 9; the established VOS related-work discussion is largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a tracking subsection, renumbers Visualization, and locally reorganizes the additional-benchmark discussion. Wording refinements include replacing long-term compatibility with capability and correcting the description of the three-point average improvement. Most existing prose and the overall structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 9, restructures Table 4 around duration and aggregate J&F scores, and adds a GFLOPs column to Table 5. It also adds a title icon and relocates Figure 3. All three figures retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports assessment of applicability and cost through tracking evaluations, a short-video case showing no gain, and explicit computational measurements in Tables 4, 5, and 9. These provide a modest benefit beyond v1's already substantial VOS evidence. Table 4 loses separate J/F detail, and the blanket superiority wording is insufficiently qualified given the new tie, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the useful added evidence.
